channel.title: Simply Explained by Suraj — Cybersecurity in Plain English
channel.description: Plain-English cybersecurity for everyone — seniors, youngsters and families first. Scam calls, passwords, updates, and the habits that keep a household safe online.

item.title: Passwords You Can Actually Live With
item.description: The safest password is not the one that looks like a cat walked across the keyboard. It is the one that is long, different for every account, and kept somewhere safer than memory.

item.title: “USPS Couldn’t Deliver Your Package” Text? The Redelivery Fee Is a Scam
item.description: It looks like a helpful note about a parcel. It is actually a thief holding out a card machine — and the defence takes ten seconds and costs nothing.

item.title: The Teammate Who Isn't Twelve
item.description: The friendliest voice in your child's game may not belong to a child at all. How game chat became a doorway — and the household rules that close it without closing the game.

item.title: The Call That Isn't Your Bank
item.description: The name on the screen says your bank. The voice says act now. Almost everything about that call is a lie — here is how the trick works, and the three habits that defeat it every time.

item.title: The Flaw Was Hiding in the Compression Library
item.description: A tiny program that unpacks compressed web data — built into websites, apps and tools you use every day — had a mistake in it. In October it went from discovery to confirmed attacks in six days. Here is what happened, in plain English.

item.title: Ransomware Still Walks In Through the Front Door
item.description: A ransomware gang breached more than 600 organizations in two years — not by breaking in, but by logging in. The same front door exists in every home. Here is how it works, and how to lock yours.

item.title: The Warning List Arrives Late. Don't Wait for It.
item.description: The US government keeps a list of software flaws that criminals are confirmed to be using. In October, attackers moved on one flaw within two hours — and the official list caught up eight days later. That gap is not just a problem for IT departments. It lives in every phone and laptop at home.

item.title: Find the Task Everyone Silently Suffers Through
item.description: Every security program has one: the recurring chore everyone dreads and nobody questions. Here's how to spot it — and why retiring it matters more than the minutes it saves.

item.title: Your POA&M Is Not a Spreadsheet Graveyard
item.description: Plans of Action & Milestones die the same way everywhere: a workbook nobody trusts, updated in a panic before the auditor arrives. It doesn't have to work that way.

item.title: Learn to Script Before You Learn to Buy Tools
item.description: The security industry will happily sell you a platform for every problem. The engineers who stay in demand learn to solve the problem first — usually with forty lines of code.

item.title: Evidence Collection Is a Pipeline, Not a Fire Drill
item.description: If your audit evidence comes from screenshots taken the night before, you don't have an evidence problem — you have an architecture problem. Here's the fix.
